conflicts.fact: Group number notation for nitrogen (and elements with 5 to 7 outer electrons) differs between lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 places nitrogen in Group 15 (and O in Group 16, also 'Group 15/V'); Lessons 3 and 4 place nitrogen in 'Group 5' and non-metals in 'Groups 6 and 7'. The two group-numbering systems (1-18 vs 1-8) are mixed without reconciliation, and Lesson 4 says the anion charge is 8 minus group number.

conflicts.fact: Phosphate valency/charge in DAP and the identity of the anion
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says (NH4)2HPO4 has subscript 2 on ammonium because 'phosphate's valency (2)' criss-crosses with ammonium's 1, and lists the radical as PO4³⁻ (valency 3). Lesson 6 uses HPO4²⁻ with valency 2. Lesson 8 says phosphate carries a 3- charge. Lesson 5 itself is inconsistent, as PO4³⁻ is 3 but the DAP explanation uses 2.

conflicts.fact: Formula of ammonium phosphate related to DAP
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7's equation 4 produces (NH4)3PO4 and calls it 'related to DAP', and the predict task asks if DAP could be (NH4)3PO4. Lessons 5, 6 and 8 insist DAP is (NH4)2HPO4 with fixed ratio. The balanced equation also does not support the fixed DAP formula Lesson 7 claims it proves.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the cumulative atomic model was begun in
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1, 3, 4, 5, 7 say it was begun in Lesson 1; Lesson 6 says it was 'begun in Lesson 2' and 'since Lesson 2'. Lesson 2 itself says it extends the models begun in Lesson 1.

conflicts.fact: Hydrogen/lithium electron data and elements in the Lesson 1 model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 covers seven elements (H, C, N, O, Na, Cl, Ca) and Lesson 2 says learners return to Lesson 1 models of H, Li, Na and K, elements Lesson 1 never included (Li, K). Lesson 2 strip A also says H is '2,1', which conflicts with H having 1 electron.

conflicts.fact: Group 1 to 3 cations list and which elements Lesson 3 covered; Lesson 4 revisits 'Lesson 3 cards' for Na, Mg, Al, Cl, O, Ca
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 evidence used Na, Cl, Ca, N, He, Ne, Ar and the 20-card sort; Mg, Al, O were not covered. Lesson 4 also calls Na, Mg, Al, Cl, O, Ca 'six elements that appear directly in the CAN and DAP formulae', but Na, Mg, Al and Cl are not in either formula. Lesson 4's simulation assigns K⁺ and N³⁻, not in the listed six.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 1 states the 2-8-8 shell model and that CAN contains the formula Ca(NO3)2·NH4NO3, while Lesson 6 tasks only NH4NO3 and (NH4)2HPO4 and says to decode 'CAN'
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 Tier 3 writes NH4NO3 as the CAN formula part and never derives Ca(NO3)2·NH4NO3 as a whole, whereas its summary says learners decode CAN [Ca(NO₃)₂·NH₄NO₃]. Lesson 8 says chart includes 'NH4NO3 or (NH4)2HPO4' as fertiliser compounds.
